canonical_name: ERFA 2.0.1 -- Essential Routines for Fundamental Astronomy (the liberally-licensed derivative of IAU SOFA)
lineage: The IAU Standards Of Fundamental Astronomy library (Wallace et al., 2000-): precession-nutation (IAU 2006/2000A), Earth rotation, time scales (TAI/TT/UT1/TDB), star-independent astrometry, ephemerides -- relicensed as ERFA (2013) so astropy could ship it. Precision-heavy by construction: the test program t_erfa_c checks every routine against reference values to ~1e-12.
version: v2.0.1 (2024), from the GitHub release tarball (autotools-generated)
entry_points: eraPnm06a, eraApci13 (astrometry), eraDtf2d/eraTaitt (time scales), eraEpv00 (Earth ephemeris); src/t_erfa_c.c (the validation program)

example.input: the reference values compiled into t_erfa_c
example.output: 't_erfa_c validation successful' -- every routine within its tolerance (ORACLE-backed)

upstream_docs: IAU SOFA Board, SOFA Astrometry Tools / Time Scale and Calendar Tools
Wallace & Capitaine, Precession-nutation procedures consistent with IAU 2006 resolutions, A&A 2006

human_capability_summary.built_to: transform positions and times between celestial reference frames to microarcsecond and nanosecond consistency
human_capability_summary.pressure: telescope pointing and ephemeris demands where 1e-9 relative error is visible; standards that change (IAU 2000/2006) and must remain reproducible
human_capability_summary.success_means: every routine reproduces the IAU reference values to its stated tolerance

known_human_problem_solved: fundamental astronomy computations to standards precision
human_environmental_pressure: extreme precision requirements, evolving standards, long time baselines
human_failure_condition: a nutation or time-scale term off by 1e-9 misplaces a star by milliarcseconds in a survey catalogue
behavioral_entry_point: perturb a constant in a copy of one routine and re-run make check: the validation names the routine that drifted

nyx_handoff.how_to_run_it: recipe.json (runner docker); python -m techne.fossils.harvest run erfa-2.0.1
nyx_handoff.what_humans_used_it_for: transform positions and times between celestial reference frames to microarcsecond and nanosecond consistency
